name: Li She
bio: Li She is dated by Giles to the 9th century AD. Giles prints two of his poems, one of them on highwaymen.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Escape
poems.author: Li She
poems.text:
Confusion overwhelming me, as in a drunken dream,
I note that spring has fled and wander off to hill and stream;
With a friendly Buddhist priest I seek a respite from the strife
Arid manifold anomalies which go to make up life.

poems.title: On Highwaymen
poems.author: Li She
poems.text:
The rainy mist sweeps gently o'er the village by the stream,
When from the leafy forest glades the brigand daggers gleam

And yet there is no need to fear or step from out their way,
For more than half the world consists of bigger rogues than they!

poems.title: 登山 (Deng shan)
poems.author: Li She
poems.collection: 千家詩 (Poems of a Thousand Poets)
poems.text:
終日昏昏醉夢間，忽聞春盡強登山。
因過竹院逢僧話，又得浮生半日閒。
